29. FINANCIAL RISK MANAGEMENT
The Group is exposed to three main types of financial risk
credit and counterparty risk -
liquidity risk -
market risk -

This note presents details of the Group's exposure to each of these risk areas, its risk management objectives, policy and procedures, and the methods it uses to measure the risks. No changes were made in the Group's approach to managing risks in 2022.

The Board of Directors is ultimately responsible for defining the Group's risk appetite, establishing risk, management policies and overseeing the Executive Board. It is assisted in these tasks by the Audit Committee, whose role is to oversee the internal control of financial reporting, risk management, and compliance with the laws and regulations. The Internal Audit department reviews the effectiveness of risk management procedure and internal controls, the results of which are reported to the Audit Committee.

The Risk Management department operates independently and reports directly to the Chair of the Board of Directors. It is responsible for identifying, assessing, mapping and monitoring the Group's risk exposure.
Credit and counterparty risk

Credit and counterparty risk represents the risk of financial loss when a customer or counterparty to a financial instrument fails to fulfil its obligations. This risk mainly concerns the item 'Trade and other receivables'.

Compagnie Financière Tradition SA is an interdealer broker in the financial and non-financial markets, serving a predominantly institutional clientele. This broking business consists of facilitating contact between two counterparties to a trade, and receiving a commission for services rendered. The Group's exposure to credit risk is therefore limited to its own claims in connection with these activities. The quality of counterparties is evaluated locally by subsidiaries in accordance with Group guidelines, and commission receivables are closely monitored. Provisions for impairment losses on receivables are recognised where necessary.

Some Group companies act as principal in the simultaneous purchase and sale of securities for the account of third parties. These trades are managed through clearing houses on the basis of cash against delivery of securities. The period between the transaction date and the settlement date is usually two days, during which Compagnie Financière Tradition SA is exposed to counterparty risk.
This risk is contained within the limits set by the Credit Committee. The Committee bases its decisions on the creditworthiness of the counterparty, taking into account ratings published
Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements

by recognised bodies (External Credit Assessment Institutions (ECAI)), and available financial information (stock market prices, credit default swaps, yields in the secondary bond markets, etc.). Where no external rating is available, the Group calculates a rating using based on an internal methodology. In addition to the counterparty's rating, the type of instruments traded and their liquidity are also taken into account for determining the limit.

Compliance with set limits is monitored independently by the Group's Risk Management department, or by the risk management departments of the operating regions. The limits are reviewed regularly, at set frequencies or following events that could affect the creditworthiness of the counterparty or the environment in which it operates (country, type of sector, etc.). Exposure is mainly concentrated in regulated financial institutions, the majority of which have investment grade ratings.

The clearing itself is handled by specialised teams. It is conducted through Compagnie Financière Tradition SA's indirect subsidiary, Tradition London Clearing Ltd, which is the pivot for the Group's matched principal transactions for Europe and Asia. Tradition London Clearing Ltd. is responsible for following up trades introduced by the Group's operating entities until their final settlement in the clearing houses. Tradition Securities and Derivatives Inc., one of the Group's US subsidiaries, is responsible for settlement of all matched principal operations in the United States. This company is a member of the FICC (Fixed Income Clearing Corporation), a central settlement counterparty for US government securities. Membership in the FICC considerably reduces the risk of a counterparty default, since it guarantees settlement of all trades entering its net.
Liquidity risk

Liquidity risk arises when the Group encounters difficulty in meeting its financial obligations. For risk management purposes the Group separates this risk into two types - transactional liquidity risk and balance sheet liquidity risk.

Transactional liquidity risk concerns the Group's ability to meet cash flows related to matched principal trades or the requirements of market counterparties, for instance, the need to fund securities in the process of settlement or to place margin calls or collateral with clearing houses or banks which provide clearing services to the Group. These liquidity demands are hard to anticipate but are normally short term, overnight or even intra-day and are usually met from overdrafts with the clearing entity. In order to manage these risks the Group ensures that its subsidiaries engaged in matched principal trading hold cash or cash equivalents sufficient to meet potential funding requirements using a statistical approach based on historical data, which is stress tested to establish an appropriate level of contingency funding.

Balance sheet liquidity risk is the risk that a Group entity will be unable to meet its net working capital needs over a certain period of time due to trading difficulties or significant investments in the business. To manage this risk, the Group's main operating entities prepare rolling twelve-month cash flow forecasts as part of the monthly financial reporting process in order to identify any potential liquidity issues.
At the very least, all entities retain sufficient cash or cash equivalents to meet expected net cash outflows for the next three months.

Controls are carried out on a timely basis to identify funds which are surplus to local requirements for up-streaming to the Group's holding companies, where working capital or structural cash requirements are identified and addressed. At the holding company level, the Group has set up financing via bond issues and a credit facility (disclosed in Note 20) which strengthens its cash position and its ability to manage liquidity risks.
Market risk

Market risk is the risk that the fair value or future cash flows of a financial instrument will fluctuate due to changes in market prices and affect the Group's net profit or the value of its financial instruments. Market risk includes currency risk and interest rate risk.
The Group's international presence exposes it to currency risk. This risk arises when subsidiaries conduct transactions in a currency other than their functional currency. Transactions are

It is dealt with on a timely basis depending on economic trends and conditions, with the exception of the UK which has adopted a systematic approach to hedging the main foreign currencies through forward exchange contracts.

The Group's exposure to interest rate risk arises mainly from the structure of its financial debt. However, since the debt is mostly fixed rate, this risk is very marginal. Financial debt commitments within the Group must be approved by the Board of Directors.
Capital management
The Group's capital management strategy aims to maintain sufficient equity to ensure operating continuity and produce a return on investment for shareholders.

The Board of Directors monitors return on equity, which is defined as the ratio of net operating income to shareholders' equity, net of the share of non-controlling interests. The Board also monitors dividends paid to shareholders.

The Group manages the capital structure and adjusts it in response to changes in economic conditions. In order to maintain or adjust the capital structure, the Group may adjust dividends paid to shareholders, return capital to shareholders, issue new shares, or sell assets to reduce debt. No changes were made in the Group's approach to managing capital in 2022. Compagnie Financière Tradition SA is not subject to any externally imposed capital requirements. However, on the local level, the main Group subsidiaries are subject to capital requirements imposed by regulators in the countries concerned. Monitoring and compliance with regulatory directives are the responsibility of local compliance officers. Subsidiaries operate in compliance with the regulatory requirements as defined by local regulators.

information_blocks.information_block: This section outlines the cash flows generated from the company's core business operations. The total net cash flows from operating activities for the year 2022 amounted to CHF 135,728,000, compared to CHF 64,165,000 in 2021.

information_blocks.subject_core_entity: Profit before tax for the year
information_blocks.information_block: The profit before tax for the year 2022 was CHF 120,069,000, an increase from CHF 85,003,000 in 2021. This figure represents the earnings of the company before tax expenses are deducted.

The depreciation and amortisation expenses for the year 2022 were CHF 26,569,000, slightly down from CHF 26,704,000 in 2021. This expense reflects the allocation of the cost of tangible and intangible assets over their useful lives.
The net financial result for the year 2022 was CHF 8,899,000, compared to CHF 9,122,000 in 2021. This figure includes all financial income and expenses.

information_blocks.subject_core_entity: Share of profit of associates and joint ventures
information_blocks.information_block: The share of profit from associates and joint ventures for the year 2022 was a loss of CHF 29,592,000, compared to a loss of CHF 22,582,000 in 2021. This reflects the company's share of profits or losses from its investments in associated companies.
The increase in provisions for the year 2022 was CHF 2,690,000, down from CHF 17,252,000 in 2021. This line item reflects changes in the company's provisions for liabilities.
The increase in deferred income for the year 2022 was a decrease of CHF 30,000, compared to a decrease of CHF 365,000 in 2021. This represents income received before it is earned.
The expense related to share-based payments for the year 2022 was CHF 1,125,000, compared to CHF 1,014,000 in 2021. This expense reflects the cost of equity compensation to employees.
There were no gains on the disposal of companies in 2022, while in 2021, there was a loss of CHF 13,235,000. This line item reflects the financial impact of selling subsidiaries.
The losses on disposal of fixed assets for the year 2022 were CHF 61,000, compared to gains of CHF 9,000 in 2021. This reflects the financial impact of selling or disposing of fixed assets.

information_blocks.subject_core_entity: (Increase)/decrease in receivables/payables related to matched principal and account holder activities
information_blocks.information_block: The change in receivables/payables related to matched principal and account holder activities for 2022 was a decrease of CHF 48,000, compared to an increase of CHF 8,729,000 in 2021.
The increase in working capital for the year 2022 was CHF 30,674,000, contrasting with a decrease of CHF 23,670,000 in 2021. This reflects changes in current assets and liabilities.
The provisions paid in 2022 amounted to CHF 1,409,000, compared to CHF 2,419,000 in 2021. This reflects cash outflows related to provisions.
The interest paid for the year 2022 was CHF 10,214,000, compared to CHF 9,264,000 in 2021. This represents the cash outflow for interest on debts.
The interest received for the year 2022 was CHF 1,209,000, compared to CHF 482,000 in 2021. This reflects the cash inflow from interest on investments.
The income tax paid for the year 2022 was CHF 14,153,000, compared to CHF 12,615,000 in 2021. This represents the cash outflow for income taxes.

information_blocks.subject_core_entity: Net cash flows from investing activities
information_blocks.information_block: The net cash flows from investing activities for the year 2022 were CHF 62,066,000, compared to a negative cash flow of CHF 65,955,000 in 2021. This section summarizes cash flows related to investments.
The acquisition of financial assets in 2022 amounted to CHF 9,045,000, compared to CHF 69,625,000 in 2021. This reflects cash outflows for purchasing financial assets.

information_blocks.subject_core_entity: Proceeds from disposal of financial assets
information_blocks.information_block: The proceeds from the disposal of financial assets in 2022 were CHF 69,500,000, compared to CHF 425,000 in 2021. This reflects cash inflows from selling financial assets.

information_blocks.subject_core_entity: Acquisition of companies, net of cash acquired
information_blocks.information_block: The acquisition of companies, net of cash acquired, in 2022 was CHF 7,138,000, with no comparable figure for 2021.
The acquisition of property and equipment in 2022 was CHF 3,565,000, compared to CHF 2,852,000 in 2021. This reflects cash outflows for purchasing physical assets.
The purchase of intangible assets in 2022 was CHF 2,224,000, compared to CHF 3,669,000 in 2021. This reflects cash outflows for acquiring intangible assets.
The dividends received in 2022 were CHF 15,597,000, compared to CHF 13,545,000 in 2021. This reflects cash inflows from investments in other companies.

information_blocks.subject_core_entity: (Increase)/decrease in unavailable cash and cash equivalents
information_blocks.information_block: The increase in unavailable cash and cash equivalents in 2022 was a decrease of CHF 1,059,000, compared to a decrease of CHF 3,837,000 in 2021.

This section outlines the cash flows related to financing activities. The net cash flows from financing activities for the year 2022 were a negative CHF 177,700,000, compared to a positive cash flow of CHF 10,310,000 in 2021.
The increase in short-term financial debts in 2022 was CHF 8,000,000, compared to CHF 3,000,000 in 2021.
The decrease in short-term financial debts in 2022 was CHF 110,000,000, compared to CHF 15,000,000 in 2021.
There was no increase in long-term financial debts in 2022, while in 2021, it was CHF 79,584,000.
The lease liabilities paid in 2022 were CHF 16,334,000, compared to CHF 13,932,000 in 2021. This reflects cash outflows for lease obligations.
The increase in capital for the year 2022 was CHF 75,000, compared to CHF 229,000 in 2021. This reflects cash inflows from capital contributions.
The acquisition of treasury shares in 2022 was CHF 18,168,000, compared to CHF 4,092,000 in 2021. This reflects cash outflows for buying back shares.

information_blocks.subject_core_entity: Proceeds from disposal of treasury shares
information_blocks.information_block: The proceeds from the disposal of treasury shares in 2022 were CHF 384,000, compared to CHF 272,000 in 2021. This reflects cash inflows from selling treasury shares.
The dividends paid to non-controlling interests in 2022 were CHF 3,877,000, compared to CHF 2,641,000 in 2021.

Name: - Insurance contracts
Effective date: 1 January 2023
This standard relates to the accounting for insurance contracts and is effective from 1 January 2023.

Standard: IFRS 17 (amendments)
Name: - Insurance contracts
Effective date: 1 January 2023
These amendments to IFRS 17 also pertain to insurance contracts and share the same effective date of 1 January 2023.

Standard: IAS 8 (amendments)
Name: - Definition of Accounting Estimates
Effective date: 1 January 2023
These amendments clarify the definition of accounting estimates and are effective from 1 January 2023.

Standard: IAS 1 (amendments)
Name: - Disclosure of Accounting Policies
Effective date: 1 January 2023
This amendment focuses on the disclosure of accounting policies and is effective from 1 January 2023.

Standard: IAS 12 (amendments)
Name: - Deferred Tax related to Assets and Liabilities arising from a Single Transaction
Effective date: 1 January 2023
These amendments address deferred tax related to assets and liabilities arising from a single transaction, effective from 1 January 2023.

Standard: IAS 1 (amendments)
Name: - Classification of liabilities as current or non-current
Effective date: 1 January 2024
This amendment pertains to the classification of liabilities and will take effect on 1 January 2024.

Standard: IAS 1 (amendments)
Name: - Non-current Liabilities with Covenants
Effective date: 1 January 2024
This amendment addresses non-current liabilities with covenants and is effective from 1 January 2024.

Standard: IFRS 16 (amendments)
Name: - Lease Liability in a Sale and Leaseback
Effective date: 1 January 2024
These amendments relate to lease liabilities in a sale and leaseback transaction and will be effective from 1 January 2024.

This block summarizes the Consolidated reserves from the table, with values in CHF 000. At 1 January 2021, the total consolidated reserves were 529,172. information_blocks.information_block: The table titled 'Proposed Appropriation of Available Earnings' presents the available earnings for the years 2022 and 2021 in CHF 000. The total available earnings for 2022 are 123,167, while for 2021, they are 160,577. This total represents the sum of retained earnings carried forward, net profit for the year, and movements in the reserve for treasury shares.

The retained earnings carried forward for the year 2022 amount to 119,097 CHF 000, an increase from 74,865 CHF 000 in 2021. This figure reflects the cumulative profits retained in the company after dividends have been paid.

The net profit for the year 2022 is reported as 15,053 CHF 000, a decrease from 80,941 CHF 000 in 2021. This figure indicates the company's profitability after all expenses have been deducted from revenues.

information_blocks.subject_core_entity: Movements in the reserve for treasury shares
information_blocks.information_block: The movements in the reserve for treasury shares show a negative value of -10,983 CHF 000 for 2022, compared to a positive value of 4,771 CHF 000 in 2021. This reflects changes in the company's treasury shares during the respective years.

information_blocks.subject_core_entity: APPROPRIATION OF 2021 AVAILABLE EARNINGS AND PROPOSED APPROPRIATION OF 2022 AVAILABLE EARNINGS
information_blocks.information_block: The appropriation of available earnings for 2021 and the proposed appropriation for 2022 includes a dividend of -40,781 CHF 000 for 2022 and -41,480 CHF 000 for 2021. This section outlines how the available earnings are allocated.
The dividend for the year 2022 is proposed at -40,781 CHF 000, while for 2021, it was -41,480 CHF 000. This represents the amount distributed to shareholders from the company's profits.

The retained earnings carried forward after the appropriation for 2022 is 82,386 CHF 000, down from 119,097 CHF 000 in 2021. This figure indicates the amount of earnings retained in the company for future use.
The legal reserve from capital contributions is not specified in the table for both years 2022 and 2021, indicating that there may be no movements or allocations in this category.
The amount available on the balance sheet for 2022 is 1,132 CHF 000, a decrease from 5,108 CHF 000 in 2021. This figure represents the available funds that can be utilized by the company.
The report a nouveau for both years is consistent at 1,132 CHF 000 for 2022 and 2021. This figure indicates the amount of earnings that are carried forward to the next accounting period.
